title: Why quicksand can't pull you all the way under
subject: quicksand
description:
Would you stay calm or panic? 👇

Movies taught us quicksand swallows people whole. A 2005 Nature study by physicist Daniel Bonn showed you stop around your waist, but getting your foot back out is another story.

Sources: Khaldoun, Eiser, Wegdam & Bonn, "Liquefaction and flow of wet sand," Nature 437, 635 (2005); Nature News, "Quicksand can't suck you under" (Sep 28, 2005); National Geographic, "Quicksand Science: Why It Traps, How to Escape" (2005); Europhysics News 37(4), 18-19 (2006).

scenes.text: Step into quicksand, and you'll stop at your waist.
Physicist Daniel Bonn saw warning signs near Namak Lake in Iran and took a sample home.
Quicksand is about 2 grams per milliliter. You're about 1, so you float.
Move, and it turns liquid, then packs tight around your legs.
In his 2005 study, freeing one foot at 1 centimeter per second took the force of lifting a medium-sized car.
Bonn's fix: wiggle your legs slowly so water seeps in. The real killer is the tide.
